description: DAVE automatically creates energy-network models by combining open sources with expert rules. The authors describe a Python implementation generating GIS-based power and gas-transmission networks compatible with network-simulation tools. The provider is Fraunhofer IEE and DAVE authors. Coverage: The model is configured for an area of interest and available source coverage. Reference dates and asset accuracy vary with the upstream datasets. Access: The public technical paper describes the tool and its data-generation process. Neither source datasets nor generated networks were downloaded. Licence and cost: The article describes the software as open source. Its publication licence must not be assumed to license every upstream dataset or software component. Limitations: The article identifies thermal and gas-distribution generation and fused-data quality descriptions as future work. Those functions are not claimed as currently available here. For simulation it prepares network models when operator data are unavailable. Related resources: model-pandapipes is a related network-simulation resource; DAVE prepares network representations, not validating every derived attribute.
